C39.content_en:
Ways to check search intent — and how the main tools compare

When you write an affiliate article, it matters whether the searcher is about to buy or just looking things up. Enter keywords one per line and this tool returns the search intent per keyword as a table.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.012 for 3 keywords and $0.072 for 500 (measured). Above 1,000 it splits automatically (up to 5,000)Intent for several keywords in a table. Intent names are translated. Save as CSV
Semrush Keyword OverviewSubscription (see the official site for plans)Labels intent as informational, navigational, commercial or transactional (per Semrush's help)
Ahrefs Keywords Explorer (Intents)Subscription (see the official site for plans)Shows search intent (see the official site)
Reading the results yourself (by hand)FreeRead intent from whether the top results are comparison articles or official sites

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Check the intent of many keywords together. Sort article ideas into buyers and researchers.
  • Four intent names. Informational, Commercial, Transactional and Navigational (shown in the page language).
  • About $0.012 for 3 keywords and $0.072 for 500 (measured). Up to 1,000 go in one request; more are split automatically (up to 5,000).
  • A few seconds. We measured under 1 second for the call.
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want how sure the intent is → the API returns a probability, but this table does not show it.
  • You have keywords with mixed intent → only the strongest intent is shown. For example, "wireless earbuds cheap" came back as commercial at about 72% probability (measured in the US).
  • You assume the same verdict as other tools → the four names match Semrush's, but each tool makes its own judgement, so the same keyword can come out differently.
  • You cannot choose a country, only a language (the API accepts a language only).

This tool does one thing: show the search intent of several keywords with plain names.

FAQ

What do the four intents mean?

Informational (wants to know), Commercial (comparing before buying), Transactional (wants to act) and Navigational (looking for a specific site).

Is "Commercial" the same as buying?

No. It is the research stage before buying. Buying is "Transactional".

Why is the probability not shown?

The tool tabulates only the intent name the API returns.

How many keywords can I enter?

DataForSEO's spec says up to 1000. We confirmed up to 3 here.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C42.content_en:
Ways to see what genres a competitor's site is strong in — and how the main tools compare

Before a sales call, it helps to know which topics the other company's site is strong on in search; it gives you a way in. Enter a domain and this tool lists, up to 100 rows, each category the site appears in, with its keyword count and estimated traffic.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.024 per call for 100 rows (measured)From a domain: keyword count and estimated traffic per category. Category names come from a free reference list. Save as CSV
Looking at their site yourself (by hand)FreeShows what they sell. Not how they are found in search
SimilarwebSubscription (its pricing page lists a Starter plan from $125/month)A service that estimates site traffic and more (see the official site for features)
Ahrefs Site Explorer / Semrush Organic ResearchSubscription (see the official sites for plans)Research the keywords and pages a site shows up for. Semrush has a topics report (see the official sites)

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • See the site's search strengths. For target.com, the biggest category (ID 10021) had about 1.17 million keywords and about 4.7 million in estimated traffic (measured).
  • About $0.024 per call. About 40 per $1, so you can research several prospects.
  • A few seconds. 1.5 seconds in the sample (measured).
  • Category names are shown. They are in English.
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want the company's industry → categories are the API's own classification, not the company's sector.
  • You want category names in another language → names come in English with the ID. If the free reference list cannot be fetched, only the ID is shown.
  • You want real visit counts → Estimated traffic (ETV) is a modeled estimate from rankings and search volume (per DataForSEO), not measured visits, and the calculation may be updated (see the official site).
  • Unnamed classes such as "Unknown" can also appear (seen in a test in Japan with suumo.jp).

This tool does one thing: show up to 100 categories a domain appears in, with keyword counts.

FAQ

Where do the category IDs and names come from?

The IDs come from the main API call. The names come from a classification list DataForSEO publishes for free (in English). Fetching that list costs nothing.

What is "estimated traffic"?

Estimated traffic (ETV) is a modeled estimate from rankings and search volume (per DataForSEO), not measured visits, and the calculation may be updated (see the official site).

Can I see more than 100?

No. target.com had 3,035 categories in total (measured).

What do country and language change?

The market for the numbers. The sample uses the United States and English, so the numbers are for US search results.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
